title: Training-kit review before packing
titleZh: 裝箱前教學套件驗收報告
passage:
A review of the first training kits turned up two issues on the same tablet: one in the draft instructions and one during practice. For the boxed kits, the diagram must show the factory profile N6 in left-handed mode and the adapter with its release button on top. Left-handed mode swaps the functions of tablet keys, not parts of the adapter. Our editor can continue showing old key positions until the profile is loaded into practice mode. For the workshop exercises, the input dot lights as soon as the tablet detects a press, before the exercise decides whether to pass it through to a shortcut. The triangle in the exercise toolbar means taps are being demonstrated without running their shortcuts. We logged another packing check for the two batches of stands. The spare foot supplied for these kits has a shallow notch. An earlier foot from stock has a smooth edge. The two parts look alike in the tray and weigh the same.

Of the three earlier drafts, J showed N6 and the adapter correctly but was made in the editor. K had the correct adapter and profile N6 loaded in practice mode, but it showed right-handed operation. L showed left-handed practice mode, but with profile M6. On our repeat test with N6 in left-handed practice mode, one shortcut was assigned to a key on the opposite side from the position in J, but the adapter release button stayed on top. Zuri used that test to prepare the replacement drawing, Z7. We tried the approved picture on this shipment’s support card. Its release-button label fell under the clip’s top bar. Below the bar there is room for the full picture on either side of the opening that shows the tablet's serial number. Moving the centered drawing straight down would run it across that opening. The top bar extends across the whole card. At final inspection we copy the full serial number through that opening, with the clip still fitted. On the first fit check, the blue mounting position left the full number readable. In the white position, the edge of the clip hid its last character.

During the rehearsal, a learner pressed the key that normally opened the magnifier in her own setup. The magnifier did not open. The recording shows the input dot lighting and the triangle still in the toolbar. We needed the station for the next class, so a trainer ended the exercise, chose “N6” from the lesson menu, and pressed the same key. The magnifier opened this time.

Evan already signed the Z7 proof at its current size; use that file on the job slip. The press can place it without altering the art or scale. The clip maker allows either of two mounting positions, marked blue and white. Switching between them moves the short retaining tab to the opposite side. The packing photo shows the blue position from behind the card, with the top edge still at the top of the photo. The tab tip extends through the card, masking the lower-left space in that rear view. Check the next proof in the clip with the printed face toward you and the card upright. The weight check was fine on both batches. Someone also attached a sharp photograph of a notched foot to the East batch’s packing record. I recognized the bench in the photograph: it had been taken to show the part pickers what to look for, before any East kits were assembled.

One point to check before we close the training issue: the learner had loaded her saved copy from Personal Profiles. The lesson menu always opens a fresh copy of our standard N6. Both display the name “N6,” but changing one does not change the other. No one reopened the learner’s copy after ending the exercise. The West batch has a less tidy record: a short clip shows the first stand being packed. The top of the foot is hidden by the packer’s hand. Just before the foot goes in, she slides it into the check slot. With the smooth foot the same slot’s pin sits flat; it rises only when it catches in the notch. In the West clip it rises. We didn’t film the rest of the West batch.
passageZh:
首批教學套件的驗收在同一台繪圖板發現兩個問題：一個出在說明草稿，另一個是在練習時出現的。盒內示意圖必須呈現原廠 N6 設定檔的左手模式，且轉接器的釋放鈕須畫在頂邊。左手模式會互換繪圖板按鍵的功能，不會改變轉接器上的零件位置。在練習模式載入設定檔前，編輯器可能仍顯示舊的按鍵位置。 教學練習時，繪圖板偵測到按鍵便會點亮輸入指示燈，早於練習程式決定是否把按鍵訊號傳給快捷功能。練習工具列的三角形表示目前只示範按鍵，不執行快捷功能。 我們也記下兩批底座的裝箱檢查。這批套件的備用腳墊上有一道淺缺口；庫存較早的腳墊邊緣是平的。兩種零件放在零件盤裡看起來相近，重量也相同。

先前三份草稿中，J 的 N6 與轉接器畫得對，卻是在編輯器中製作的。K 的轉接器無誤，也在練習模式載入了 N6，但呈現的是右手操作。L 採左手練習模式，卻用 M6 設定檔。我們用 N6 的左手練習模式重測，有一項快捷功能被指派到草稿 J 所示位置另一側的按鍵，但轉接器釋放鈕仍在頂邊。祖莉依這次測試繪製了替換圖 Z7。 我們在本批說明卡上試裝已核准的圖。固定夾的頂部橫桿遮住了釋放鈕標示。橫桿下方有一個開孔，可看到繪圖板序號；開孔左右各有足夠空間放下整張圖。如果把原本置中的圖面直接下移，就會跨到開孔。頂部橫桿橫跨整張卡片。 最終檢查時，固定夾仍裝著，我們會透過開孔抄下完整序號。第一次試裝時，固定在藍色標記位置能讀到整個序號；裝在白色標記位置時，夾子的邊緣會遮住最後一碼。

預演時，學員按下在自己的設定中通常用來開啟放大鏡的按鍵。放大鏡沒打開。錄影中，輸入指示燈有亮，工具列上的三角形也還在。下一堂課需要用這座工作臺，教學人員就結束練習，從課程選單選了「N6」，再按下同一個鍵。這一次放大鏡打開了。

伊凡已簽核目前尺寸的 Z7 校樣；工單請使用該檔。印刷時可以移動圖面位置，不必改圖或改大小。製造商允許固定夾有兩種安裝位置，分別標為藍色與白色。換到另一位置時，短卡舌會移到對側。包裝照片從卡片背面拍攝的是藍色位置，卡片頂邊仍在照片上方。卡舌尖端穿過卡片，遮住從背面看的左下區域。下一張校樣請裝進固定夾，再將卡片直立、印刷面朝向自己進行檢查。 兩批的重量檢查都沒問題。有人也在東批的裝箱紀錄中附上一張清楚的缺口腳墊照片。我認出了照片裡的工作臺：那是東批開始組裝前，為了讓備料人員知道要找哪個零件而拍的。

結束追蹤教學問題前，有一點要先確認：學員當時從「個人設定檔」載入自己儲存的版本。課程選單每次都會另開標準 N6 的副本。兩者都顯示「N6」，但變更一份不會影響另一份。練習結束後，沒有人重新開啟學員的版本。 西批的紀錄比較不整齊：一小段影片拍到第一個底座裝箱。裝箱人員的手遮住了腳墊上方；她在放入前先把腳墊滑進檢查槽。平邊腳墊進槽時，槽上的檢查銷會維持平放；只有卡入缺口時才會升起。西批影片中檢查銷升了起來。我們沒有拍西批其餘套件。
